title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs about? What undergoes rebirth? Because of what is there no liberation? - Craving gives birth…
content:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs about?
What undergoes rebirth?
Because of what is there no liberation?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind itself always runs about,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Because of suffering, there is no liberation.

title: Four wheels, nine doors, Full of defilement, tied by greed — Mired in mud, O great hero, What will be the future state Of such…
content:
Four wheels, nine doors,
Full of defilement, tied by greed —
Mired in mud,
O great hero,
What will be the future state
Of such a human birth?

(The Blessed One):
Having cut off delight and bondage,
Sensual desire and evil,
Having destroyed the root of craving —
Such will be his future state.

title: Elder Sabbhakāma: This two-footed creature, Impure and foul-smelling, Full of various corpses — From it, fluid oozes. With deer, use a trap; with fish, a…
content:
Elder Sabbhakāma:

This two-footed creature,
Impure and foul-smelling,
Full of various corpses —
From it, fluid oozes.

With deer, use a trap; with fish, a hook;
With monkeys, a pit;
Thus worldlings are caught.

Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, touches —
Agreeable and pleasing —
These five strands of sensual pleasure
Are known in female form.

Worldlings, with mind infatuated,
Run after enjoying female form.
The terrifying cemetery increases,
Storing up renewed existence.

One who avoids female form
As a foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one overcomes
The world’s poisoner.

Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures,
Security in renunciation,
Having escaped all sensual pleasures,
I have attained the destruction of defilements.

title: “Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has conscience (hiri): he is ashamed of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, ashamed of evil, unwholesome states. He has…
content: “Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has conscience (hiri): he is ashamed of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, ashamed of evil, unwholesome states. He has fear of wrongdoing (ottappa): he fears bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, fears evil, unwholesome states.”

title: “Monks, whatever is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. And what, monks, is not yours? The eye, monks,…
content: “Monks, whatever is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. And what, monks, is not yours? The eye, monks, is not yours — abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. Forms are not yours — abandon them. Eye-consciousness is not yours — abandon it. Eye-contact is not yours — abandon it. Suppose, monks, a person were to carry away, burn, or do whatever they want with all the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves in this Jeta’s Grove. Would you think: ‘This person carries us away, burns us, or does whatever they want with us’?” - “No, venerable sir.” - “Why not?” - “Because that is not our self nor belonging to our self.” - “So too, monks, the eye is not yours — abandon it … Forms … Eye-consciousness … Eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that feeling is not yours. Abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being.”

title: - “Venerable Sāriputta, what things should a virtuous monk attend to wisely?” - “Venerable Koṭṭhika, a virtuous monk should attend wisely to the five aggregates…
content: - “Venerable Sāriputta, what things should a virtuous monk attend to wisely?” - “Venerable Koṭṭhika, a virtuous monk should attend wisely to the five aggregates of clinging as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as empty, as not-self. What five? The form aggregate of clinging, the feeling aggregate of clinging, the perception aggregate of clinging, the formation aggregate of clinging, the consciousness aggregate of clinging. Venerable Koṭṭhika, a virtuous monk should attend wisely to these five aggregates of clinging as impermanent … as not-self.”

title: “Monks, there are these five mental shackles. What five? Here, monks, a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual…
content: “Monks, there are these five mental shackles. What five? Here, monks, a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual pleasures. Monks, for a monk who is not free from lust … craving for sensual pleasures, his mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving. If one’s mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving, that is the first mental shackle.”

title: “Monks, just as in the last month of the rainy season, in autumn, when the rice has ripened, a cowherd tending cows would poke the…
content: “Monks, just as in the last month of the rainy season, in autumn, when the rice has ripened, a cowherd tending cows would poke the cows on this side and that with a stick, restraining and checking them. Why is that? Because the cowherd sees that otherwise there would be death, imprisonment, beating, or blame. Monks, even so, I saw the peril, the degradation, the defilement of unwholesome states, and I saw the escape, the benefit, the purification of wholesome states.”

title: “Abandon desire, abandon greed — These are the bonds of worldlings. The one with eyes walks the path, Crosses hell and human birth. Eating little,…
content:
“Abandon desire, abandon greed —
These are the bonds of worldlings.
The one with eyes walks the path,
Crosses hell and human birth.

Eating little, moderate in food,
With few wishes, not greedy —
He is without desire, without craving,
Truly at peace.

Having gone on alms-round,
The sage enters the forest,
Goes to the root of a tree,
Prepares his sitting place.

The wise one, meditating,
Delights in the forest,
Meditating at the root of a tree,
Content, he practices his own pleasure.”

title: “Hearing the Buddha’s words, The wise monk fully understands the body, Sees it as it really is. As it is below, so above, As above,…
content:
“Hearing the Buddha’s words,
The wise monk fully understands the body,
Sees it as it really is.

As it is below, so above,
As above, so below —
Abandoning desire for the body inside and out,

The wise monk abandons desire and lust.
He attains the deathless, peace,
The constant state of Nibbāna.

This two-footed, impure, foul-smelling body
Filled with various rotting corpses, oozing —
Yet it is preserved and honored.

Who would think to exalt this body,
Or despise another —
Except one who is blind?”
